story: Anthropic-linked Public First Action gives $3m to PAC backing Scott Wiener (San Francisco Standard, 13 Oct 2026)

item.title: AI group pours millions into race for Pelosi's seat. Its pick: Scott Wiener
item.curator_note: Anthropic-linked Public First Action gave $3 million to a PAC backing Scott Wiener for Nancy Pelosi's House seat; AI money becomes a campaign issue.

entry.headline: A group backed by Anthropic donations has put $3 million behind Scott Wiener's bid for Nancy Pelosi's House seat, making AI money a campaign fight.
entry.summary: The San Francisco Standard reports that Public First Action, a group that campaigns for AI safeguards and has received two $20 million donations from Anthropic, the San Francisco maker of the Claude chatbot, gave $3 million since August to a political action committee backing state Sen. Scott Wiener, the author of California's AI safety law, in the race for Rep. Nancy Pelosi's seat; Punchbowl News first reported the donation. At a debate on 13 Oct his rival, Supervisor Connie Chan, said the AI industry is bankrolling him, while Wiener insisted "there is no Anthropic money in this race", and Anthropic says its gifts can fund only education and policy work, though the group has not said who pays for its political spending.
entry.importance_line: AI regulation is now a deciding issue for San Francisco voters choosing Pelosi's successor on 3 Nov, and the fight over who funds candidates reaches AI firms such as Anthropic, though whether any Anthropic money reached the race is disputed and the group's political donors are undisclosed.
entry.notes: Written from WORKDIR/fulltext/P01.txt. Donation first reported by Punchbowl News; SF Standard confirmed it with a Public First Action spokesperson and reported the debate itself, so it is credited as source with Punchbowl named. Status CONFIRMED on the spokesperson's confirmation of the donation; the claim that Anthropic money funds the race is disputed and kept as each side's claim. Not a reply story.

entry.headline: An AI-safety group tied to Anthropic has put $3 million behind Scott Wiener in the race for Nancy Pelosi's House seat.
entry.summary: The San Francisco Standard reports, citing a spokesperson for the group and a donation first reported by Punchbowl News, that Public First Action, an advocacy group that pushes for AI safeguards and has received two $20 million gifts from Anthropic, has given $3 million since August to a PAC supporting state Sen. Scott Wiener against Supervisor Connie Chan for Nancy Pelosi's seat in the 3 Nov 2026 election. At a debate on 13 Oct 2026 Chan said voters cannot trust a candidate "bankrolled by the AI industries" to regulate it, while Wiener replied that "there is no Anthropic money in this race", and Anthropic says its donations to the group may be used only for education and policy work, not campaigns.
entry.importance_line: AI money is now the main argument in the contest for Pelosi's seat, which affects San Francisco voters first and then any candidate taking AI-linked support, though whether Anthropic's own money reached the race is contested and the group has not named its political donors.
entry.notes: The Standard credits Punchbowl News with first reporting the donation but confirmed it itself and reported the debate, so The Standard is the source and Punchbowl is named inside. The reader-level and format rules were read; no conflict found.
